subject: ACME VPC: IDP provisioning & SCIM bridge design
messages:
From: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: idp-admin@acme.com, security-admin@acme.com
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SCIM provisioning for VPC-isolated control plane

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. A couple things we need to confirm before we give infra the green light for the private control plane:

- SCIM provisioning: our corporate IdP (Okta) will not be able to reach Redwood's hosted SCIM endpoint directly over the public internet due to our egress policy. We were thinking about a short-lived SCIM bridge deployed in our VPC to mute that requirement.
- Group-to-role mapping: we want AD groups mapped to Redwood IAM roles (admin, operator, readonly) and want the ability to scope roles per VPC project.
- SAML assertions: our SAML contains an "entitlements" attribute with multiple group DNs; we'd like to avoid custom parsing if possible.
- Audit evidence: security wants proof of provisioning events and SCIM delta logs pulled into our SIEM.

I've attached a draft attribute map and our VPC diagram. Can you confirm the recommended flow, and whether Redwood supports a customer-hosted SCIM proxy + short-lived credentials to the control plane?

Appreciate it,
Kevin

Attachments:
- acme-scim-attribute-map.csv (CSV)
- acme-vpc-network-diagram.pdf (PDF)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme.com>
Cc: idp-admin@acme.com, security-admin@acme.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning for VPC-isolated control plane

Kevin —

Thanks for the notes and the attachments. High level we can support the design you described. Proposed approach (summary):

1) SCIM bridge in customer VPC: deploy a lightweight SCIM proxy (container) in ACME's VPC that listens on a private subnet. The proxy forwards normalized SCIM v2 calls to Redwood over an mTLS tunnel (Mutual TLS) with customer-managed short-lived client certs. This avoids exposing SCIM endpoints publicly.

2) Role mapping: the proxy performs attribute translation using a configurable map (your CSV). We recommend ACME map group DNs to Redwood role identifiers and include a project tag attribute for scope ("redwood:project_id").

3) SAML -> session: SAML assertions still authenticate users to ACME IdP; when a user is provisioned/updated, SCIM writes the group membership. For immediate access (no SCIM roundtrip), we support a signed SAML assertion exchange flow where the IdP can post an assertion to Redwood's control plane via an API endpoint over the same mTLS tunnel.

4) Audit logs: the bridge will send provisioning events to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) and also mirror an obfuscated delta log to Redwood for cross-checking. Redwood can mask PII, retain event IDs, and surface them in the Console.

Next steps:
- Marcus (cc'd) will own the technical runbook and the cert rotation plan.
- Can ACME infra provision a private endpoint (ENI) reachable from the bridge container?
- Please confirm the group->role mapping in the CSV and highlight any multi-tenant project needs.

I'll loop in Olga from our security team to review the mTLS and key management approach.

Best,
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, idp-admin@acme.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning for VPC-isolated control plane — runbook + cert plan

Thanks Kevin / Mina. A few operational clarifications from the infra side: 

- Certificate lifecycle: we propose issuing a short-lived client cert (X.509) scoped to the bridge container, renewed via ACME-style API every 24 hours. The cert is presented by the bridge when calling Redwood's private ingest endpoint. Redwood will validate via our client CA.
- Firewall and egress: the bridge needs outbound connectivity to Redwood's private control plane endpoint on TCP 443. If ACME blocks outbound to external IPs, we can arrange a peered VPC endpoint or use a reverse TLS connection initiated by Redwood to a listener in ACME VPC (we discussed both options in the call).
- Role scoping: inside the SCIM mapping we add a claim redwood:project_id and recommend enforcing RBAC at the control plane layer (project-scoped role bindings). We should document whether a single group can map to multiple projects — recommendation: avoid unless explicitly required.

Action items I will own:
1) Draft the cert rotation API sample (OpenSSL + automated curl).
2) Provide a hardened container image for the SCIM proxy with limited surface area.
3) Produce a sample SIEM forwarder config.

Kevin — can your team confirm whether you prefer daily cert rotation vs. cert-on-demand? For high security customers daily is standard for us.

Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: idp-admin@acme.com, security-admin@acme.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SCIM provisioning for VPC-isolated control plane — security notes

Kevin —

A few security guardrails from our review team: 

- Key management: we require customer-managed KMS for the SCIM bridge private key; Redwood will accept public key uploads for validation and will not store private material. If ACME cannot use a KMS, we will need an HSM-backed escrow arrangement and an SOC attestation.
- Least privilege: the SCIM bridge service account should be limited to PATCH/PUT for user/group resources only. No delete rights for automated processes without a manual approval step.
- Immutable audit: provisioning deltas forwarded to Redwood must include an event ID and HMAC (shared secret exchanged during setup) so events cannot be tampered with in transit.
- SAML assertion endpoints must require nonce + timestamp and replay window of <= 30 seconds.

I'll attach a short checklist (see Drive link) for the compliance packet we will need to collect: cert CNs, KMS ARN, SIEM ingestion endpoint, expected RTO for provisioning reconciliation.

Regards,
Olga
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme.com>, idp-admin@acme.com, security-admin@acme.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME VPC: IDP provisioning & SCIM bridge design — confirmation and next steps

Kevin / team —

Thanks for confirming last week. Quick summary and plan we agreed on during the call today: 

1) Deployment model: ACME will deploy the SCIM proxy in a private subnet. The proxy will use customer-managed KMS for private key operations and rotate certs daily via the cert-rotation API Marcus will provide.
2) Networking: ACME will provision an ENI with route to Redwood's peered endpoint; if peering isn't available we will use pull-based reverse TLS as fallback.
3) Identity mapping: Kevin to produce a finalized CSV mapping file with group DNs -> redwood_role and redwood:project_id columns. We will validate the file and run a dry-provision in our staging tenant.
4) Logging and evidence: ACME SIEM endpoint will receive raw deltas, and Redwood will store hashed event IDs. A reconciliation job will run every hour and produce a reconciliation report to your security mailbox.

Attached are: the draft runbook (link in Drive) and the attribute map you sent with a few comments.

Next calls:
- Technical cutover: Thu 29 Jan 2026 10:00 PST (proposed) — Marcus to lead.
- Compliance sign-off: Tue 3 Feb 2026 14:00 PST — Olga + ACME security.

If that schedule works, please confirm and upload the finalized CSV.

Regards,
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- acme-scim-attribute-map.csv
- acme-vpc-network-diagram.pdf
